reciprocal.into: Feed the belly, not the eye
reciprocal.link: D024 — Guard your senses from overload
reciprocal.why: Both principles draw on Daodejing chapter 12: D024 takes its warning about the five colours and five notes overloading the senses, and D025 takes the sage's answer, satisfying the belly rather than the eyes.

reciprocal.into: Need little — one branch, one belly of water
reciprocal.link: Feed the belly, not the eye
reciprocal.why: D105's wren and mole take only what fills the belly, and D025 names the same contrast between need and appetite from Daodejing chapter 12.

reciprocal.link: D094 — Don't exhaust yourself for what you don't need
reciprocal.why: D094's Zhuangzi chase story is about pursuing what is not needed until the pursuit itself harms the pursuer, the state of unrelieved effort that this concept studies.

reciprocal.into: Travel light: drop the excess baggage
reciprocal.link: D101 — Drop pretense — stop standing on tiptoe
reciprocal.why: Both principles come from Daodejing chapter 24's tiptoe passage: D101 takes the bodily image of standing on tiptoe as pretense, and D103 takes the same passage's self-display and self-assertion as weight carried for show.
